Alex —

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. Our security team asked for more granularity on two items in the RFP: 1) a segregation matrix that shows tenant/network boundaries and control ownership across the stack, and 2) a short assessment of cascade/failure-resilience between zones (how we prevent a failure in an inference shard from widening to other tenants or control plane components).

Can you provide a single packet with the matrix, an annotated topology diagram, and a short threat-summary? Ideally the packet also calls out where hardware/region failover and cross-zone fallbacks occur. We have an internal deadline of next Friday (06/27).

Hi Lydia —

Appreciate the specificity. Attaching a consolidated packet with: a segregation matrix XLSX, an architecture snapshot PNG annotated for blast-radius lines, and a 2-page threat model summary PDF. Short answers below; full packet is attached.

Quick highlights:
- Segregation: logical tenant isolation at the inference fabric layer (per-model serving pods) plus network microsegmentation at the host and subnet level. Control plane (auth, model registry) sits in a separate sealed subnet with limited egress and HSM-backed key material.
- Cascade resilience: per-zone circuit breakers (token/resource-based) and request-level isolation via request queues and prefix KV isolation — we run automatic rollback to a lower-capacity replica in a different AZ if KV state is unavailable.
- Control ownership: table in the XLSX maps controls to teams (Serving Runtime, Control Plane, Network).

Attachments: segregation-matrix-v1.xlsx, network_topology_v3.png, threat-model-summary-2025-06.pdf

Cc'ing Kim and Mina for any additional technical artifacts or clarifications. If you'd like a short walkthrough, we can do a 30-minute call — propose Thu 06/19 10:00am PT.

Best,
Alex Martinez

Lydia —

Adding a few clarifications from an architecture perspective (pulled from the attached summary PDF):
- Tenant-level isolation: we use per-tenant namespaceing with enforced RBAC and a hardened execution sandbox that strips out outbound network policies by default. Tenant workloads run on GPU pools that are logically pooled but physically tagged; we enforce strict kernel-level isolation and cgroup constraints to prevent noisy-neighbor resource exhaustion.
- Network demarcation: control plane endpoints are reachable only from our operator subnets via mutual TLS; data plane (inference requests) enters through an ingress tier that performs token validation and rate shaping. Egress ACLs default to deny; explicit allowlists are scoped per customer and documented in the matrix.
- KV / prefix caching: KV caches are sharded per-tenant with namespace prefixes and per-shard quotas. When a cache shard is degraded, the request path can fallback to a cold read from the model store but requests are circuit-broken after a configurable latency/p95 threshold.

We included an annotated attack-path diagram (see PNG) that marks where we expect fail-open risk and mitigations. Happy to walk through.

Kim Park
Senior Security Architect — Redwood Inference

Lydia —

Answers below, short bullets as requested: 
1) Artifact provenance:
- network_topology_v3.png — derived from our canonical Diagrams folder (Drive) and exported by the architecture team weekly; master files are in the Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0BzCrescent/segregation-evidence
- segregation-matrix-v1.xlsx — generated from our compliance repository (automated export) but contains hand-reviewed owner mappings; we include generated CSVs in the evidence bundle and an XLSX with reviewer notes.
- threat-model-summary-2025-06.pdf — compiled by Security (manual edits) but versioned in the compliance repo.

2) Automatic rollback triggers & KV reconciliation:
- Triggers: health-check failures (P95 latency > configured threshold), persistent error rates on the inference shard (>=5% request error for >60s), or operator-initiated isolate/evacuate actions.
- Mechanism: when a rollback is triggered the serving runtime flips routing to a replica in a different AZ/zone; the KV cache for the affected tenant stays read-only and falls back to cold reads from the model store. A reconciliation job then performs warm-up of the new replica's cache with a safe prefetch window (rate-limited). For strong consistency requirements, customers can opt into write-through backing stores that maintain durable state independent of the cache.

3) Evidence delivery SLA:
- For audit requests we provide a standard evidence packet within 5 business days for hosted customers (includes logs, diagrams, and generated exports). Expedited 48-hour delivery is available under an enterprise support addendum. Procurement can reach out to procurement@redwood.com for formal SLAs and pricing.

Confirming network_topology_v3.png is an export of the canonical Drive source; we will include the source diagram file on request.

Mina Haddad
Principal Product Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
